title: Telemetry Sliceboard: streaming vs non-stream latency decomposition by model & route
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Build a reusable telemetry sliceboard that decomposes latency by model and route with explicit streaming vs non-streaming breakouts. This ticket covers instrumentation additions (trace tags and structured logs), metric ingestion/schema changes (histogram/t-digest settings), log/metric pipeline transformations, dashboard panels (p50/p95/p99 + cohorting), and runbook updates for alerts. Primary audience: platform SREs and product engineers who need to triage tail latency and regressions when model variants or IO modes change. Key constraints: minimal added cardinality to primary metrics, end-to-end trace links from dashboard cohorts, and parity between streaming and non-stream panels for side-by-side comparison.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard contains per-model/per-route panels for p50, p95, p99 with a toggle or paired view for streaming vs non-streaming
Each latency datapoint links to representative distributed traces (trace ID) and a short sample log for the request
Metrics pipeline produces a model_route.io_mode histogram metric with consistent bucket/t-digest configuration and <=5% ingestion overhead on busy routes
Tracing instrumentation adds deterministic attributes: model_name, route, io_mode (streaming|sync), request_shape (tokens_in, tokens_out), and inference_variant
Dashboards include cohort slicer (by request_shape, client, release tag) and historical comparison for regressions by day/week
Alerting playbook updated: p99 spike > 2x baseline for 10m triggers paging with runbook link and rollback guidance
implementation_notes: Instrumentation: Add io_mode tag on all server span roots and on the response span. Use canonical values 'streaming' and 'sync' to avoid cardinality issues.
Tracing hooks: emit a short 'sample-summary' span that includes tokens_in/tokens_out and quantization_profile to quickly identify heavy requests without sampling full payloads.
Metrics: introduce metric name rp.latency.histogram with labels model_name, route, io_mode, service_zone. Use t-digest aggregation in metrics pipeline and export p50/p95/p99 downstream.
Metric buckets: keep exponential buckets for fast tails; validate final p99 accuracy against raw traces on a 24h sample before rollout.
Logs: enrich request logs with structured fields request_id, trace_id, io_mode, tokens_in, tokens_out, and inference_variant. Mark high-latency samples with 'latency_cohort' tag.
Pipeline: update Kafka topic schema for enriched metrics; add a lightweight transform that pivots streaming fragments into a single logical request for accurate latencies.
Storage: store precomputed aggregates for the last 90 days and raw t-digest sketches for on-demand re-aggregation to support cohort queries.
Dashboard: implement paired-pane layout: left column sync, right column streaming. Panels per model-route row with p50/p95/p99 sparkline + anomaly banding overlay.
Trace linking: attach a top-3 slow trace sample link per cell by querying trace index keyed by latency_cohort and trace_duration desc.
Backwards compatibility: provide a legacy 'io_mode=unknown' fallback when older agents don't emit the tag; filter these for migration reporting.
Performance guardrails: add rate-limited trace sampling for high-volume routes and live validation that metric emission cost stays below 5% of baseline.
Privacy/compliance: ensure logs sampled for examples scrub prompt content; only tokens counts and truncated anonymized metadata flow to observability stores.
